thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 — High error rate detected for org=orionhealth. Alerting on-call. Summary: sustained 429/503 spike, request QPS up ~8x, increased KV cache misses. Triage channel: #incidents.

marta (oncall-sre): on it. paging now. anyone seeing obvious config changes?

lee (eng-runtime): seeing a surge in token generation requests from orionhealth tokenset. 90th p90 latency up from 120ms -> 1.8s. 429s up to ~18% on their traffic.

nora (oncall-ml): model-side CPU/GPU looks okay but queue depth is high on host pool-a. Looks like one org is hogging concurrent streams.

sam (eng-platform): can we throttle at the routing layer quickly? we have per-org overrides.

marta (oncall-sre): want to do immediate mitigation — reduce orionhealth throughput while we root cause. propose set org QPS -> 3 and concurrency -> 2 for 10m then reassess. opinions? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

lee (eng-runtime): yes agree. this preserves platform SLO for other customers. add a short customer notice via support once stable.

jordan (support): i'll prep a short, honest note for orionhealth: "we detected high sustained traffic from your workspace and temporarily throttled to stabilize service; investigating; will follow up".

marta (oncall-sre): executing mitigation now. running admin CLI:
```
# admin console
rictl org-rate override set --org orionhealth --max-qps 3 --max-concurrency 2 --ttl 600 --reason "hotfix spike 1785432100"
```

ops-bot: Command accepted. Override scheduled, id=ovr-7f9a. Applying to routing layer...

ops-bot: Done — override active. Effective QPS=3, concurrency=2 for org=orionhealth.

lee (eng-runtime): metrics check: total platform QPS dropped 12%, 429s platform-wide dropped to baseline. orionhealth 429s jumped temporarily as requests were throttled (expected).

nora (oncall-ml): latencies recovering on pool-a. queue depth down 60%. good signal.

sam (eng-platform): I'm leaving a temporary circuit-breaker rule: if orionhealth error-rate > 25% for >2m, escalate to full block. Pushed rule in prod.

marta (oncall-sre): next: need to decide root cause action — spike could be legitimate customer load or runaway client loop. Jordan pls contact customer. Ask for traffic pattern and whether they rolled out a change.

jordan (support): reaching out now. pinging Orin (customer eng) and ops@orionhealth.

jordan (support): update: customer says they launched a new batch job at 07:40 that fan-outs ~20k requests. They didn't expect this magnitude.

lee (eng-runtime): that matches our traces — many short-lived connections with identical session keys. Looks like a parallel retry storm.

marta (oncall-sre): since it's customer-caused, keep the throttle in place and schedule a controlled whitelist if they can coordinate reduced batch size. Jordan — request a mitigation plan and ETA.

jordan (support): asked for ETA, suggested a rollback or progressive ramp. waiting reply.

sam (eng-platform): we should also add a temporary quota bite to their org page so they can self-serve to see limits. low friction.

lee (eng-runtime): FYI, we also turned on short-term prefix caching for their frequent prompts to reduce KV misses: config at route layer:
```json
{"org": "orionhealth", "prefix_cache_ttl": 60, "cache_policy": "aggressive"}
```

marta (oncall-sre): good. monitoring for 10m. set alert if platform-wide error rate rises or if their throttle saturates >95%.

ops-bot: alert rule updated.

nora (oncall-ml): watching model quality metrics — no regression so far.

jordan (support): customer replied — they paused the job and will re-run with rate limiter baked in, ETA 30m. thank you note.

marta (oncall-sre): status update: mitigation holding. leaving override for now but will reduce duration to 300s if customer confirms job paused.

lee (eng-runtime): log snippet showing the applied rule and hits:
```
2026-03-15T07:46:12Z route: apply_override ovr-7f9a org=orionhealth qps=3 conc=2
2026-03-15T07:46:18Z route: throttle hit org=orionhealth token=abc... count=423
```

sam (eng-platform): also documenting action in incident tracker. we should create a follow-up to add an automated safety: detect >5x org QPS spike and auto-notify customer with suggested limits.

marta (oncall-sre): agree. create GH issue after this thread.

jordan (support): customer confirmed pause. will coordinate a staged restart with us and keep us posted.

ops-bot: override ovr-7f9a ttl updated to 300s = expires at 1785432400.

marta (oncall-sre): passing to night on-call in 30m. handoff notes: applied temporary throttle to orionhealth (QPS=3, conc=2), waited for customer to pause job; watch for auto-escalation if throttle saturates or platform errors increase.

nora (oncall-ml): added to handoff: monitor model pool-a queue length and p95 latency.

lee (eng-runtime): I'll follow up tomorrow with trace sample and recommended per-org guardrails.

marta (oncall-sre): thanks team. I'm closing the active mitigation after override expires and customer confirms restart plan. leaving this thread for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 status -> mitigated (partial). Created postmortem stub: PM-1785432100.
